title: Introduce cross-sdk credential consensus and stream-sentinel retry profiles
author: Priya K. Menon
description:
Motivation: We observed subtle inconsistencies in credential selection and retry behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs when the platform returns mixed TTLs and transient auth failures under load. These divergences led to duplicated token exchanges and increased tail latency for streaming consumers. This PR introduces a lightweight, cross-language design called "credential consensus" plus a streaming retry orchestration pattern named "stream-sentinel" to align behavior across SDKs, reduce redundant reauths, and provide deterministic backoff/abort semantics for long-lived streams.

What this PR does in one paragraph: Adds a consensus window and voting heuristic to credential selection so concurrent consumers converge on a single reauth path, implements a stream-sentinel that centralizes heartbeat/failover logic for streaming handles, harmonizes retry preset profiles across SDKs (fast-retry for short-lived unary calls, sentinel-backed adaptive backoff for streams), and bumps SDK package versions to capture the new API and bugfixes (python 0.12.0, typescript 1.8.0, go 1.5.2).

Design notes and rationale: Credential consensus: each SDK exposes a short-lived in-memory lease cache with a consensus epoch id. When a renewal is required, the first process to propose a renewal writes a proposal token to the local lease store; others observe the proposal and attach to the resulting token rather than racing. This reduces N-way token swap storms seen in high-concurrency serverless deployments. Stream-sentinel: streaming clients obtain a lightweight sentinel handle that owns heartbeat scheduling and initiates sentinel-heard fallback (switch to fallback credential or model variant) on sustained failures. The sentinel encapsulates abort hooks, recommended backoff profiles, and a visibility layer for observability.

Compatibility and ergonomics: The APIs are additive. Existing constructors gain an optional "credConsensusConfig" (defaults to off for historical parity but enabled in our SDK bundles for Redwood-hosted usage). Stream-sentinel is opt-in via "streamOptions.sentinel: true" for minor releases; the default in this PR for pre-bundled SDKs is enabled to reduce incidents in production. Migration notes are included below.

Testing and QA: Unit tests added for all three SDKs (consensus election, proposal expiry, sentinel failover paths). Integration tests run against a local dev harness that simulates mixed-ttl auth responses and concurrent stream attach/detach. Benchmark run: 2x reduction in auth-exchange rate under 200 concurrent clients in our perf-canary lab; 20% median tail improvement for long-lived streams under error injection. E2E staged rollout: feature-flagged on staging for 48 hours, then progressive rollout to 10%/50%/100% groups controlled by console toggle.

Rollout plan and observability: Feature gated via env var REDWOOD_SDK_CRED_CONSENSUS and REDWOOD_SDK_STREAM_SENTINEL. Console dashboard includes new metrics: sdk.cred.consensus.proposals, sdk.cred.consensus.attach_rate, sdk.stream.sentinel.fallbacks and sdk.stream.sentinel.heartbeat_misses. Alerts: increased sentinel fallback rate >1% triggers P1 channel.

Developer notes: - Python: introduces redwood.session.consensus module and SessionClient.consensus_config. - TypeScript: new CredConsensus class in @redwood/sdk-core and optional stream.sentinel flag on StreamHandle options. - Go: cred/consensus package and StreamSentinel struct with attach semantics. All three SDKs export a small diagnostics hook for troubleshooting (max 8KB JSON).

Upgrade guidance: Non-breaking by default. For teams that already implemented custom token rotation, set REDWOOD_SDK_CRED_CONSENSUS=off and keep existing behavior while validating sentinel in a subset of clients. See UPGRADING.md entries added to each SDK package for code samples.

Security review: This PR went through security review (Mei Chen) to ensure no credential material is persisted to disk and all leases are ephemeral and truncated to KMS-backed keys where present.

Related work: builds on ENG-3421 (reduce auth storms) and ENG-3490 (streaming resilience).

review_comments: Rafael Ortega (reviewer): The consensus proposal TTL needs to be conservative to avoid single-proposer lockouts in noisy environments. Can we make it adaptive based on svc latency?
Priya K. Menon (author): Agreed. Implemented adaptive TTL that increases with observed auth latency; default remains 250ms but grows up to 2s under heavy auth latency (see consensus.py lines 78-104).
Mei Chen (security): Verified no secrets persisted. Please add a short fuzz test for proposal injection vectors.
Priya K. Menon (author): Added fuzz test in tests/integration/consensus_harness.py and documented attack surface in SECURITY_NOTES.md.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Nice. Two nits: (1) rename StreamSentinel.Attempt -> StartAttempt for clarity, (2) add an example to UPGRADING.md showing a streaming handler using sentinel.fallback().
Priya K. Menon (author): Addressed both nits; renamed and added example code snippets in UPGRADING.md for each SDK.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge by Mei Chen on 2026-03-01. Changelog: 'sdk: cross-sdk credential consensus + stream-sentinel retry profiles; bump versions py 0.12.0 / ts 1.8.0 / go 1.5.2'.
release_notes: Added cross-language credential consensus to reduce concurrent token exchanges; introduced StreamSentinel to improve streaming resilience and unify retry behavior across SDKs. SDK version bumps: python 0.12.0, typescript 1.8.0, go 1.5.2. Feature gated with environment flags; consult UPGRADING.md for migration steps.
backport_notes: Backport candidates: release/1.4.x (go), release/0.11.x (python). Changes touch core retry surfaces; require manual cherry-pick of consensus election code and UPGRADING docs.
testing_summary: Unit tests (py/ts/go) covering consensus election, TTL adaptation, sentinel failover paths added. Integration harness exercised mixed-ttl auth responses and 200 concurrent stream clients. Perf canary results attached. All CI green after one lint fix iteration.
notes_for_release_team: Coordinate staged rollout with Console team to enable REDWOOD_SDK_CRED_CONSENSUS toggle. Ops should monitor sdk.cred.consensus.proposals and sdk.stream.sentinel.fallbacks during rollout. Inform SRE on first 10% step.
